description: Added 2026-07-28 at maintainer request. Whenever an agent fleet is spawned (background subagents, parallel waves, Workflow orchestration), a summarised progress update MUST be posted in chat at least every 15 minutes until the fleet finishes. Rationale: silent stretches let the remote execution container idle out, and a timed-out container loses in-flight work. Codified as a new mandatory section in CLAUDE.md ('Agent-fleet progress reporting'), placed after 'Workflow rules'. Requires: never go quiet while agents run (post even a no-news update); summarise rather than dump transcripts; schedule the heartbeat with send_later rather than relying on memory; final summary when done; relaxes no other rule (working-hours guardrail and never-auto-commit/push still bind).
title: HARD RULE: agent-fleet progress updates every 15 min (container-timeout prevention)

description:
Landed in this tranche: aster/viscochab.rs + viscochab/tests.rs -- the 27-ODE rkdcha.F90 rate system, the calsig.F90 isothermal isotropic stress update, and a strain-driven ViscoplasticChabocheSystem integrated by outram_foam_basic_lib::ode::OdeIntegrator. 11 verification tests green.

Deliberately NOT ported, each documented in the module docs:
1. The implicit NEWTON/NEWTON_RELI path (cvmres.F90 residual + cvmjac.F90 Jacobian). Would also give VISCOCHAB a Rosenbrock23-capable OdeSystem::jacobian.
2. calsig.F90 extras: thermal strain (ALPHA + TEMP fields), damage coupling, orthotropic elasticity, and the C_PLAN branch.
3. A_R (coefficient 3) is stored but unused, because rkdcha.F90 hard-codes A_R=1 while cvmcvx.F90 honours it. If the implicit path is ever ported, A_R becomes live and the two paths must be reconciled.
4. Tangent operator -- upstream offers PERTURBATION/VERIFICATION only, so nothing analytic exists to port.
5. Validation. Everything so far is verification only. astest/ssnv118a-d, ssnd105b-d, ssnd111a and ssnv226a in the upstream clone exercise VISCOCHAB and are the obvious oracle -- check DATA_POLICY scope before using them.

STILL NEEDED IN aster/mod.rs: the pub mod viscochab; line is in place, but the pub use re-export block is not (see the agent report for the exact list).

description:
crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/huang2025waterIngress.json (Huang et al. 2025, 'The water ingress analysis on steam generator heat-exchange tube rupture accident of HTGR', Ann. Nucl. Energy 211:110968, doi 10.1016/j.anucene.2024.110968) carries this copyright line:

  (c) 2024 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved, INCLUDING THOSE FOR TEXT AND DATA MINING, AI TRAINING, AND SIMILAR TECHNOLOGIES.

That is an explicit TDM/AI reservation, stronger than the plain all-rights-reserved notices on the older Elsevier papers in the archive. kovan lit import performs bulk full-text extraction into a machine-readable corpus, which is arguably exactly what the clause reserves. Full-text extraction was therefore deliberately SKIPPED at ingest (2026-08-11): the record is bibliographic metadata plus factual findings only (facts and numbers are not copyrightable expression).

DECISION NEEDED (AI_USAGE.md / DATA_POLICY.md): is full-text ingestion of TDM-reserved publications acceptable for this project? If NO, the record stands as-is and the paper is read by humans and cited normally. If YES under some rationale, the body can be extracted then.

AUDIT RESULT (librarian pass 2026-08-11): every proprietary PDF was grepped for the clause ('text and data mining' / 'AI training' / 'similar technologies'). ONLY huang2025waterIngress carries it. gao2002, wu2002, wang2014, tantillo2020, xhonneux2014, tobias1980: zero hits — their earlier full-text ingests do not retroactively violate an explicit reservation. Do not delete anything; nothing needs deleting per this audit.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-11: the metadata-only approach for huang2025waterIngress is APPROVED. Maintainer: 'I think you made the right decision on huang2025.'

So the standing rule for a document whose copyright line reserves text and data mining / AI training rights: catalogue the bibliographic metadata and the factual findings, and DO NOT run bulk full-text extraction into the corpus. The paper stays fully usable — read it, cite it, implement correlations from it, record its numbers with provenance, because facts are not copyrightable. Only the machine-readable full-text corpus is withheld.

Currently affected: huang2025waterIngress ALONE. A grep audit of all seven proprietary PDFs on 2026-08-11 found the clause in no other document; the earlier full-text ingests (wu2002, gao2002, wang2014, tantillo2020, xhonneux2014, tobias1980) carry no such reservation and need no action.

REMAINING WORK on this bead: make the rule enforceable rather than remembered. A future ingest should DETECT the reservation clause and refuse or warn, instead of relying on whoever is ingesting to read the copyright page carefully. Grep terms that caught it: 'text and data mining', 'AI training'. That check belongs next to the visibility inference in the ingestion path.

title: MAINTAINER DECISION: full-text ingestion of TDM/AI-reserved publications (huang2025waterIngress is the pending case)

description:
Maintainer reports htgr_sim_v1 still feels laggy on 2026-08-12, AFTER the pebble-bed texture bake landed (541a38ef33). Deferred by the maintainer, not pursued that day.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so this is not a duplicate of op-szmi.12:
The bake IS wired into the HTR-10 vessel -- htr10_reactor_vessel.rs:44 imports draw_bed/BedTint from components::pebble_bed_texture. Measured for that widget: 19910 shapes / 1.73 ms per frame -> 39 shapes / 0.014 ms, the bed's own share going 19874 circles -> 3 quads. So the single largest known cost is gone and the lag is something else.

THE FIRST PROBLEM IS THAT WE ARE BLIND. **htgr_sim_v1 has NO frame-time readout.** grep for GuiFrameMetrics / frame_interval / update_cpu_time in examples/htgr_sim_v1/ returns nothing. fhr_sim_v2 has had one since 2026-08-12 (four side-panel rows: update() CPU time, peak CPU, frame interval, FPS), and GuiFrameMetrics was PROMOTED to src/app_scaffold/gui_frame_metrics.rs specifically so both simulators could share it. htgr_sim_v1 was never wired to it.

DO THAT FIRST. Do not guess at a cause -- that mistake has already been made once on this exact symptom, where physics was blamed before measurement showed it was at 20% duty. The readout distinguishes:
  - small update() CPU inside a ~16.7 ms interval  -> vsync-limited, healthy, look elsewhere
  - CPU approaching the interval                   -> our ui() body is the bottleneck
  - CPU peak >> CPU mean                           -> intermittent hitching, not uniform slowness
  - long interval with small CPU                   -> cost is in egui tessellation / GPU / compositor

CANDIDATES, in rough order, NONE verified:
1. Per-frame animation now running that was not before: the turbine rotor spins from a real torque balance (00a776be12) and the schematic drives flow tracers. Both are cheap in principle; measure rather than assume.
2. The schematic composes many widgets -- vessel, steam generator, turbine, condenser, pipes, bends, legend, instrumentation. Their combined shape count has never been measured the way the vessel's was.
3. op-szmi.9's sibling defect: fhr_sim_v2 clones its whole state twice per frame. Check whether htgr_sim_v1's HtgrSnapshot clone is comparable -- it now carries ~39 fields.
4. Whether the bake is actually HITTING its cache in this simulator, or re-baking. A re-bake costs 2.4 ms and is meant to be paid once per size; if the cache key is being invalidated every frame the bake would be a net loss. This is worth checking early because it would be a defect rather than a cost.

BLOCKED ON: examples/htgr_sim_v1/ was owned by the steam-generator agent as of 2026-08-12. Wire the readout after that lands.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
2026-08-12 19:50, cross-link + unblock:

UNBLOCKED. The steam-generator agent's work landed (edbb2bd7, 1d4ac747), so examples/htgr_sim_v1/ is no longer owned. The frame-metrics wiring described here can proceed.

NOT THE SAME AS op-v5zb / op-775s, filed this evening. Keep them apart:
  - THIS bead is GUI frame time -- does update() render fast enough. Symptom: feels laggy.
  - op-v5zb is the physics thread's simulated-time-per-wall-second ratio. Symptom: plant evolves slower than real time.
A simulator can render a clean 60 fps and still advance its plant at 0.8x real time; they are independent and need separate readouts. The warning in this bead against blaming physics for a rendering symptom still stands and op-v5zb does not weaken it -- op-v5zb is evidenced from loop structure (a fixed 10 ms sleep placed AFTER the compute, app/mod.rs:118), not inferred from the lag report.

RELEVANT PRIOR DATUM: this bead records physics measured 'at 20% duty'. If that is 2.5 ms of compute against the 10 ms sleep, it implies a real-time ratio of 10/12.5 = 0.8x -- i.e. that same measurement, read against the wrong denominator, was already evidence for op-v5zb. Worth recovering the original number when op-775s runs.

title: htgr_sim_v1 still feels laggy AFTER the texture bake — and it cannot measure itself
